backbone: Build a trace family of dimension >=3 with potential automorphic support via solvable base change, find a regular classical point on it, and propagate pro-modularity back to r along connected curves.
quote: Once the second curve has potential Hecke support, localized propagation puts the entire unrestricted locus on that support.

backbone: Reduce to finite fixed-mass blocks, build projected numerator tables, and bound pair overlaps (second-moment / quasi-independence) via weighted lcm arithmetic estimates to obtain full measure.
quote: Here the transfer is proved directly for weighted finite arrays, using a virtual comparison sum and a fixed finite-union approximation to an avoided set.

backbone: Prove a stronger birational decomposition statement (semiample positive part plus negative part) by induction on dimension using Kähler MMP, special termination, boundary generation and fibration descent.
quote: This form both supports the induction and retains the line-bundle information needed for generation on the original space.

backbone: Write down explicit hypersurface ring A, exhibit explicit stabilization A[w]=C^[5] via exponential of an LND, and show A is not C^[4] by a degeneration plus derivation rigidity contradiction.
quote:
We construct an explicit integral complex affine fourfold $X$ with $X	imes\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$ but $X
ot\cong\mathbb A^4$.

backbone: Construct two explicit weighted-homogeneous Thom-Sebastiani sums of orders 2 and 3 with matching spectra, build an integral Seifert-form isometry via local-global quadratic-form arguments, then invoke high-dimensional link classification.
quote: We construct two reduced hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have multiplicities two and three.

backbone: Regularize the measure, prepare pair measures with angular projection gains (incidence/Furstenberg inputs), and bound a weighted spherical-shell oscillatory estimate to give the distance pushforward an L2 density.
quote: Mattila's spherical-average criterion~\cite{Mattila1987} made Fourier \(L^2\) estimates a central approach to the problem.

backbone: Prove a signed finite-band gradient estimate for disk-average envelopes via local disk-moment cancellation and multiscale dyadic prices summed by telescoping, then pass to Sobolev inputs by localization and limits.
quote: The masses paired at successive levels form a telescoping sum. Charging each pair at coarser observation scales with the factor $(s/r)^\alpha$ gives a nonnegative price $D_Q$ for every dyadic cell

backbone: Lift to a coefficient space with a convex body bounding all states; show via Gaussian survival that it has small Dirichlet energy for all diagonal weights, which yields signs step by step through lifted Steiner symmetrization.
quote: First, if a bounded symmetric convex body has small Dirichlet energy for every positive diagonal weight, it supports a single square root of a probability density with small derivatives in every coordinate.

backbone: Construct an explicit multitape algorithm: finite linear networks with a rank saving speed up address-chunk interchanges, giving a recursive saving in synthetic FFT layers, then exact convolution-based integer multiplication with cost analysis.
quote: We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values while restoring every auxiliary value.

backbone: Give an explicit randomized algorithm: lazily evaluated coarse seed tables on an interval tree, refined over repeated passes via entropy-regularized online choices whose regret bounds yield (1+eps) accuracy in almost-linear expected time.
quote: Recursively partition the first string into a tree of intervals, ending at intervals of length at most one.

backbone: Explicitly construct height-3 expressions over the original alphabet by encoding finite-monoid computations as affine updates recovered through successive split constructions with clocks, markers and episode decoders.
quote: We express finite-monoid computations using a prefix code of word pieces.

backbone: Assume zero exponent at arbitrarily large parameters; cancellation-scarcity and fast-bridge product estimates control growth shortfalls across dyadic lengths, and rescaled limiting distance-array measures yield a contradiction.
quote: Suppose now that arbitrarily large parameters had zero exponent almost everywhere.

backbone: Assume a proper 5-coloring; amenable averaging and Haar rigidity transfer it to a weak measurable coloring, whose angular palette structure is excluded by cases on 3-, 4- and 5-cycles (Moser spindle certificate).
quote: A simple cycle on five labels has length three, four, or five. Section~\ref{sec:angular} excludes each possibility.

backbone: Assume a bad sequence of colorings; extract discrepancy/purity regularity at power widths, then embed a monochromatic cube by probabilistic row assignments (local lemma, Hall's theorem), contradicting badness.
quote: We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main} by contradiction along sequences.

backbone: Prove a uniform little-o improvement of the activity-interval packing bound by contradiction via limiting rank-coordinate measures and transverse foliations, then iterate a contracting recurrence at a fixed scale for the power saving.
quote: We prove a uniform little-$o$ improvement of this packing bound as $n/b$ tends to infinity. Choosing one sufficiently large fixed scale then gives a contracting recurrence and the power saving

backbone: Prove a Chern-number obstruction: a small CM module on a completed section ring yields a sheaf whose Chern inequality forces K^2-2c2<=6H^2; then construct an explicit Kummer-type surface violating it.
quote: We construct a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain containing $\C$, with residue field $\C$, that has no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen--Macaulay module.

backbone: Reduce to an exponentially decaying idempotent, write each trace coefficient as a Pfaffian curvature average of a connection built from smooth multiscale summaries, and bound the curvature so only finitely many finite-order classes survive.
quote: We obtain them from smooth spatial summaries whose derivative bounds are independent of the size of the input support, multiscale time averaging with a positive translation component, and a final ordered-kernel bound uniform in the closing group element.

backbone: From imported local-law spectral inputs, prove variance-one Gaussian moments of bulk eigenvectors at sampled edges via star counting and entropy inequalities, insert Gaussians via switches, and identify the limit with GOE via Dyson Brownian motion.
quote: A colored-star counting inequality becomes an entropy inequality after the eigenvectors are smoothed by a Gaussian field.

backbone: Construct one Borel rule via stochastic localization: Brownian observations of edges with posterior-mean drift from the free spanning-tree limit, inverted deterministically using a uniform response bound, then recover the forest at large times.
quote: We prove the unrestricted graphwise statement by a different construction: the same Borel rule works for every graph in our class, independently of any random-graph law.

backbone: Construct pairs of CFI-style grid structures with opposite F3-consistency answers; symmetry and support bounds show counting equivalence, so any CPT program gives equal outputs, contradicting the opposite answers.
quote: Choose the program and its constants $q,m$ first, and then take $L$ large. Counting equivalence forces the same halt stage and output on the two structures, contradicting their opposite query answers.
